correctness.rationale: For b>0, 0<h<1 with nonzero pole denominators, the three cyclic equations reduce by elimination to fixed-point factor Q and cubic C(X)=bX³+AX²+BX−LM. Genuine primitive 3-cycles have distinct coordinates, all three simple real cubic roots, since disc(C)=t²P² with t=1−h and P an explicitly strictly-positive sum of squares. For 0<b<1, t<b(1−b), signs C(0)<0, C(h−b)>0, C(1−b)<0, C(h)>0 locate three positive roots in (0,h), and exact cyclic linear reconstruction plus resultants yields an actual orbit; exceptional b=h/(1+h) is covered by an explicit positive orbit. Conversely b≥1 gives negative Vieta coefficient B; for b<1 and t≥b(1−b), signs of B or −LM exclude three positive roots. Uniqueness follows from distinct cubic roots and unique reconstruction for a generic root. Independently symbolically checked the discriminant/sum-of-squares identity, four exact sign identities, and resultant(C,K) using SymPy; all-parameter proof uses inequalities, not sample parameters. Boundary t=b(1−b) has the known 0-coordinate nonnegative 3-cycle, not strictly positive.
